items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: Danny Gawka, a guitar player? They used to be around the taproom.

ctx.x: Yes, well almost everybody in that period that came in was a hot man. But a lot of guys found out they weren't hot enough and then they became more legit or something. For instance, I had a fellow that came to New York with me and I had room for a while. He was from Cortland, New York, which is near Syracuse. And he played so hot in the Casco Mountains that we called it the nearest thing to a torrent or trumpet that we'd ever heard. And he still played a lot of jazz, but he made his biggest mark playing in bands…

Did you know Elma and Nicholas, a clarinet player? Danny Gawka, a guitar player? They used to be around the taproom. At least they made some records with Rolini during that period. Well, there were two things that happened here.

First of all, there were so many musicians that you met. That union floor and the street around the union floor after union hours was just loaded with musicians and you don't remember, you know, you just didn't get their name or associate with them. And then the other thing that operates is the fact that I've forgotten a lot of the fellows' names. I've tried to recall in my own mind sometimes, many of the people that I work with, I can remember their face and the fact that I'm working with them better than I can…
